newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GOVERNOR REJECTS BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY'S CLAIM

Uttar Pradesh Governor Romesh Bhandari is believed to have communicated to the union government that no party was in a position to form a stable government in the State. This means the state will be put under the President's rule. Earlier in the day, the governor rejected the Bharatiya Janata Party's claim that it could form the government on grounds that it lacked the required strength.
Indian Express
PRESIDENT'S RULE LIKELY IN UTTAR PRADESH

The government may invoke Article 356 of the constitution and repromulgate President's Rule in Uttar Pradesh (UP). Repeated talks between various parties have failed to resolve the impasse in the state. No party enjoys absolute majority in the newly formed UP Assembly. President S.D. Sharma is expected to issue the proclamation after he returns from his foreign tour. The current spell of federal rule in UP ends tomorrow. The Union Cabinet is likely to clear the imposition of President's rule.
Financial Express
FIAT TEAM COMING TO FINALISE AUTO DIVISION PLAN

Italian auto major Fiat is sending a high level delegation to finalise plans for its auto division in the country. The move follows the announcement by Fiat SPA CEO P.Cantarella, who recently visited the country, to invest $1.0 billion in India. The Italian major plans to manufacture 100,000 cars in the country. It is estimated that the group will put in 15 billion rupees in its Palio car project.
RELIANCE CONSULTANCY LICENCE TO BE SUSPENDED FOR SIX MONTHS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has decided to suspend Reliance Consultancy Services (RCS), the share transfer agent of Reliance Industries, for six months with effect from February 1, 1997. RCS has been given time from October 17 to January 31, 1997 to make alternate arrangements for share-holders of the Reliance group. The suspension follows an inquiry in to improper share swaps by RCS.
CABINET TO DECIDE ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT LEVEL IN MINING

The government is planning to allow 50 percent foreign equity participation through the automatic route in the mineral prospecting and mining sectors. The Cabinet will decide the matter today. The Ministry of Mining has proposed allowing 51 percent equity on a case-by-case basis.
INDIA TO GO IN FOR NUCLEAR ENERGY IN A BIG WAY

India has decided to go for nuclear energy in a big way. The country would increase generation in this sector 10 times by the year 2020, said science and technology minister Y.K. Alagh. The minister said the decision to go for nuclear energy was taken because besides being cheap it ensured energy security. For design modifications, the government has decided to finance research in this sphere involving the industry. India has set a target for producing 20,000 mw of nuclear power by the year 2020.
The Economic Times
JUMP IN INVENTORIES JAMS CASH FLOW OF COMPANIES

The corporate sector is facing a crisis on account of mounting inventories and receivables which have cramped the flow of funds into companies. A study of the financial performance of top 200 companies in the last fiscal has shown that growing inventories and receivables consumed more than 53 percent of the total cash generated by them during the period. This possibly laid the foundation for the current slowdown in corporate growth, the study said.
Business Standard
PANEL SEEKS CHEAPER CREDIT TO REVIVE INDUSTRY

The L.M. Thapar Committee on Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), set up by Associate Chambers of Commerce and Industry, called for a level playing field for the domestic industry. The committee proposed a cut in interest rates to international levels. However, it welcomed FDI and recommended an increase in the cap on foreign institutional investment and suggested raising foreign equity cap to 75 percent from the current level of 51 percent.
SHARP SLOWDOWN IN IMPORTS OF CAPITAL GOODS

Imports in the capital goods sector have sharply declined to 9.8 percent. Combined with this, an actual decline in imports of certain capital goods components may reflect in lower growth for fiscal 1996-97 (April-March). Commerce ministry sources feel the growth rate of the five main components of capital goods-import machine tools, machinery, electrical machinery, project goods and transport equipment fell to 9.8 percent from around 20-25 percent in the corresponding earlier period. In contrast, machinery imports in April-December 1995-96 rose by 35 percent while project goods import rose by 28 percent.
The Observer
GLOBAL BIDDING INVITED FOR RURAL NETWORK

The Department of Telecommunication (DoT) has cancelled tenders for 1,300 rural telecommunication equipments and has invited global bidding for the proposed rural network. The latter fall under the Asian Development Bank (ADB) loan. The move has shocked the telecommunication equipment industry. The Telecommunication Equipment Manufacturers Association has warned that this would lead to the closure of entire equipment industry.
